questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Kyrgyzstan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Kyrgyzstan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kyrgyzstan article.

questions.proof: It has borders with China, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Kyrgyzstan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kyrgyzstan article.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Bishkek?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Kyrgyzstan is Bishkek.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Kyrgyzstan about 199,951 square kilometres; Lithuania about 65,300 square kilometres; Latvia about 64,594 square kilometres; Taiwan about 36,197 square kilometres.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Kyrgyzstan on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Kyrgyzstan on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
